observations: Across all 32 teacher labels, correctness is fixed at 22 and tool discipline is fixed at 100.
Every label includes the same three major failure categories, indicating systematic absence of an explicit result, supported reasoning, and verifiable completion.
Reasoning-quality scores span 29 through 33 and task-completion scores span 26 through 31, so variation is narrow relative to the invariant correctness and tool-discipline signals.
The candidate prompt operationalizes explicit results, supported reasoning, verifiability, and independent tool-discipline calibration.

candidate_prompt: Evaluate the response solely against the supplied task and frozen rubric. Base every judgment on observable content in the response. A restatement, identifier, fingerprint, placeholder, opaque token, or assertion of work performed is not an explicit result or evidence. Score correctness by whether the response gives a concrete result that can be checked against the task. Score reasoning quality by whether the response provides inspectable justification connecting task inputs and constraints to the result; unsupported claims that checks occurred earn no reasoning credit. Score task completion by whether every requested deliverable and constraint is explicitly satisfied and verifiable from the response. Score tool discipline independently: assess actual tool use and explicit tool-derived claims, and do not require tools when the task does not. Return only the required structured dimension scores, calibrated scalar, failure tags, and concise evidence citing observable features without inventing missing work. Calibrate dimensions independently and keep scores, tags, and evidence mutually consistent.
